title: Motifs, tapestry, amigurumi and Tunisian: crochet that sells

say: Motifs, tapestry, amigurumi and Tunisian: crochet that sells.
This is the video for module three of Advanced Knitting and Crochet.
Crochet is fast and sturdy. This module covers four families that sell well. Joined motifs make blankets and bags. Tapestry crochet makes firm pouches.
Amigurumi makes stuffed toys, and Tunisian crochet makes scarves and dishcloths with a woven look. All instructions here use US terms.
The skill is not making one square. It is making many squares the same size. In a classic granny square, round n has 4 times n clusters. If your count is different, the square will twist.
For example, Bisi in Akure makes one 4-round square, blocks it, and it measures 10 cm and weighs 9 g.

panel.heading: Bisi plans a baby blanket
items: Add 15% for joins and border: 828 g

say: The customer wants about 80 by 100 cm. That is 8 squares across and 10 down: 80 squares, and 720 g of yarn.

panel.heading: Bisi plans a baby blanket
items: Add 15% for joins and border: 828 g

say: She adds about 15 percent for joining and the border, 828 g. In 50 g balls that is 16.6, so she buys 17, all from the same dye lot. Now she can quote a real yarn cost.

panel.heading: Bisi plans a baby blanket
items: Add 15% for joins and border: 828 g
panel.rule: Measure and weigh one blocked square, then multiply.

say: A slip stitch join gives a decorative ridge. A single crochet join is firmer, good for bags that take weight.

panel.heading: Choose the join for the job
items: Slip stitch: a decorative raised ridge
Whip stitch: flat, for baby items

say: Whip stitch with a tapestry needle is flat, good for garments and baby items. Join-as-you-go attaches each square on its last round, which saves time on large blankets.
Block every square to the same size before you join, and photograph the layout first.

panel.heading: Choose the join for the job
items: Slip stitch: a decorative raised ridge
Whip stitch: flat, for baby items

say: In tapestry crochet, the colour you are not using lies along the tops of the stitches, and you crochet over it, so it is hidden.

panel.heading: Change colour and fit the chart
items: Carry colour B inside the stitches
Pull up the last A loop: 2 on hook
Finish the stitch with colour B

say: To change colour, on the last stitch in colour A pull up a loop, so you have 2 loops on the hook. Then yarn over with colour B and pull through both.

panel.heading: Change colour and fit the chart
items: Carry colour B inside the stitches
Pull up the last A loop: 2 on hook
Finish the stitch with colour B

say: For example, Zainab in Kano has a diamond motif 12 stitches wide. Her flat base adds 6 stitches each round, so round 10 has 60. 60 divided by 12 is 5 diamonds. It fits, so no motif breaks where the round starts.

panel.heading: Change colour and fit the chart
items: Carry colour B inside the stitches
Pull up the last A loop: 2 on hook
Finish the stitch with colour B
panel.rule: The round's stitch count must be a multiple of the motif width.

say: Amigurumi are small stuffed toys, worked in tight single crochet spirals with a marker at the start of each round.
Start with 6 stitches in a magic ring, and add 6 stitches every round: 12, 18, 24, 30.

panel.heading: The six-increase sphere
items: Decrease 6 per round, in mirror order
Stuff firmly, then close the last 6

say: Work plain rounds, then decrease 6 per round in the mirror order. Stuff firmly before the last round, and close it like a drawstring.
Stagger the increases each round, or the ball turns into a hexagon.

panel.heading: The six-increase sphere
items: Decrease 6 per round, in mirror order
Stuff firmly, then close the last 6
panel.rule: Stagger the increases, or the ball gets six corners.

say: Toy safety comes first. For babies and children under 3, embroider eyes and noses with yarn. Small parts that come loose are a choking hazard.

cards.d: Embroider eyes and noses with yarn. No plastic eyes, buttons or beads that can come loose.
Use new, clean toy stuffing. Sew limbs on through the body several times.
Pull each part firmly before you sell or gift it. No long cords or loops.

say: Use new, clean polyester toy stuffing, not old pillow filling or rags. Sew limbs and ears on through the body several times.

cards.d: Embroider eyes and noses with yarn. No plastic eyes, buttons or beads that can come loose.
Use new, clean toy stuffing. Sew limbs on through the body several times.
Pull each part firmly before you sell or gift it. No long cords or loops.

say: Give every toy a firm pull on each part before you sell or gift it, and avoid long cords that could wrap around a neck.

say: Tunisian crochet uses a long hook and keeps many loops on it, like a knitting needle. On the forward pass you pick up loops. On the return pass you work them off, two at a time. You never turn the work.

panel.heading: Two passes, then time yourself
items: Forward pass: pick up loops, keep them
Return pass: work them off in twos
Larger hook and a border stop curl

say: Tunisian fabric curls. Fight it with a larger hook, a loose foundation chain, a border, and blocking.

panel.heading: Two passes, then time yourself
items: Forward pass: pick up loops, keep them
Return pass: work them off in twos
Larger hook and a border stop curl

say: For example, Mercy in Benin City makes scarves of 225 rows. She times 10 rows at 25 minutes, so 2.5 minutes a row. With the border and blocking, each scarf takes about 10.5 hours. She will price from that real figure, not a guess.

panel.heading: Two passes, then time yourself
items: Forward pass: pick up loops, keep them
Return pass: work them off in twos
Larger hook and a border stop curl
panel.rule: Time 10 rows and multiply. Use real time for pricing.

say: To remember. Weigh and measure one blocked square, then multiply. Make the round count a multiple of the motif. Add 6 stitches each increase round.
Embroider features on toys for under-3s and pull-test every toy. And time yourself, so your prices use real hours.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Fit the motif into the round count
Time 10 rows to know your real hours
